response.title: Do I need the more expensive kind of battery that runs dryer-type appliances, or is a regular one enough for home backup?
response.answer:
For most homes, a regular home backup battery is enough. You only need the more expensive type that can run dryer-type appliances if you want to power large 240V appliances during an outage.

The key difference is between essential-load backup and whole-home backup.

Which type do you need?
Shop

Regular backup battery (often 120V)

Good for refrigerators, Wi-Fi, lights, TVs, laptops, and some small appliances.

Best if you primarily want to keep essentials running during a power outage.

Shop

240V-capable backup system

Can support larger appliances such as electric dryers, electric ranges, well pumps, and some central air conditioners, provided it has sufficient power output.

Best if you want your home to operate more normally during an outage.

What matters more than the battery type?

There are three important specifications:

Specification

	

What it tells you




Voltage (120V vs. 240V)

	

Which appliances the system can supply




Power (kW)

	

How many appliances can run simultaneously




Capacity (kWh)

	

How long the battery will last

For example, a 5 kWh battery might run essential appliances for several hours, but an electric dryer drawing 5 kW could consume that much energy in roughly one hour.

A 240V system also needs adequate inverter output and surge capacity. Simply having a large battery doesn't guarantee it can run a dryer or central AC.

My recommendation

I'd generally skip paying extra just to run an electric dryer during an outage. Prioritize refrigeration, lighting, internet, and cooling or heating needs. This is also consistent with guidance on sizing backup systems around critical loads. 
California Air Resources Board
+1

One important exception: central air conditioning often requires 240V, just like an electric dryer. So if keeping your central AC running is important, the more capable system may be worth it.

One question: During a power outage, do you want to keep your central AC running, or would you be satisfied with just the refrigerator, lights, internet, and a few outlets?

That distinction will help determine whether the cheaper battery is sufficient.
